about.title: City of Industry Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: City of Industry moves a lot of trucks, forklifts, and commuters through a relatively small footprint, and that mix shows up in the crash numbers: 207 injury collisions and 282 people hurt in the most recent reporting year, with 3 lives lost. Corridors like Valley Boulevard, Gale Avenue, Azusa Avenue, and Hacienda Boulevard carry heavy volume, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to see more reported crashes as workers head out. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the aftermath can be confusing — insurance adjusters calling, medical bills arriving, and no clear sense of what your claim is worth. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect injured people with independent personal injury attorneys who work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. We can help you take that first step without adding to what you're already dealing with.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Quickly After a City of Industry Crash

items.title: California's Filing Window Is Limited
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but if a government vehicle or public road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, a Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for a crash on a corridor like Gale Avenue or Azusa Avenue, you may still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. Insurers often use this rule to lowball claims, which is why guidance early on matters.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash, often before you know the full extent of your injuries. There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in California, but what you say early can still shape how an adjuster values your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in City of Industry?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your crash involved a government-owned vehicle or a road maintained by a public agency, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months. Because City of Industry has a mix of private and public roadways, it's worth confirming which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: Was the crash on Valley Boulevard or Hacienda Boulevard my fault if I was partly to blame?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible, though your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help evaluate the specifics of what happened on these higher-volume corridors.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to be cautious before giving a recorded statement, since insurers can use your early words to minimize your claim later. Speaking with an independent attorney first can help you understand what you're required to share and what you're not.
